output.summary: KEP-3721 adds the ability to populate a container's environment variables from a file, initially restricted to files in an emptyDir volume read by kubelet. Its status is implementable, targeting stable.
output.rationale: Existing ConfigMap and Secret env mechanisms need extra API calls when an initContainer produces configuration, and vendor images need env vars from files. The KEP lets kubelet read an env file from an emptyDir and instantiate the variables without mounting the file in the consuming container. Reviewers raised concerns about precedence, security of arbitrary volumes, and scope, which shaped the emptyDir-only design.

alternatives.option: Populate env vars from a ConfigMap or Secret resource
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this proposal 'allows populating environment variables from a file in container filesystem and thus reducing the need of an API call or extra permissions to kube-apiserver.'

alternatives.option: Read all variables from a file without naming them (EnvFromSource-style)
alternatives.why_not: This is listed as a non-goal: 'We do not intend to support instantiating all variables from an env file ... without knowing their names a priori.'

alternatives.option: Allow any volume type rather than only emptyDir
alternatives.why_not: Sergey Kanzhelev said emptyDir was picked because 'it doesn't have any secrets', and the thread records that expanding beyond emptyDir was not agreed for the current scope. Later proposals (ephemeral volumes) were still under discussion, not adopted.

alternatives.option: Restrict the volume source on the producer side only
alternatives.why_not: thockin argued 'A volume is a volume. We shouldn't add new restrictions on mounting it,' and suggested restricting on the consumer side instead, which the discussion accepted as making sense.

evidence.quote: Support instantiating a container's environment variables from a file. This file must be in emptyDir volume.
this proposal allows populating environment variables from a file in container filesystem and thus reducing the need of an API call or extra permissions to kube-apiserver.
Adding the "only emptyDir" restriction on the CONSUMER side makes sense.

This is why emptyDir was picked - it doesn't have any secrets. If you would to expand emptyDir, do you have some suggestions on how this can be limited to some more useful, but still secure set of supported types?
The file will be read by kubelet at container startup time. It will be re-read if the container restarts.
